key_insight: There is no universally best flow surrogate: the winning architecture depends on whether the target dynamics are boundary-driven and direct or self-sustained and phase-sensitive.
engineering_relevance: For CFD deployment, surrogate choice and validation must match the flow regime, because a model that looks good on RMSE can still fail on physically important quantities like shear stress, shedding power, or timing.
method: Compared 8 surrogate models on two transient flows with time-varying boundary conditions: CMP slurry film and Kármán vortex street.
Varied two design axes: full-field vs latent representation, and one-shot vs autoregressive time prediction.
Evaluated models with five physics-aware questions: field, structure, motion, amplitude, and timing.
evidence_signal: On CMP, a one-shot full-field model achieved 3.2% relative error in cumulative wall shear stress; on KVS, a latent autoregressive DeepONet preserved 96% of shedding power while direct and one-shot models nearly eliminated it, and surrogates were 10^3–10^4× faster per query than the finite-element solver.
watch_item: Training simulations are expensive, so the offline cost can delay payoff unless the surrogate is queried beyond the break-even point, and RMSE alone can select the wrong model.
paper_title: No Free Lunch in Flow Surrogates under Time-Varying Boundary Conditions: A Two-Regime Study
